terms.title: Selector
terms.definition: A CSS selector targets HTML elements on a page to apply styles.
terms.explanation: Selectors can target element tags, class names, IDs, attributes, and pseudo-states.

terms.title: Class Selector
terms.definition: Selects elements with a specific class attribute.
terms.explanation: Preceded by a period (.) and can be reused on multiple elements across a page.

terms.title: ID Selector
terms.definition: Selects a single element with a unique id attribute.
terms.explanation: Preceded by a hash symbol (#) and should target only one element per document.

terms.title: Specificity
terms.definition: The algorithm browsers use to determine which CSS property values are applied when multiple rules conflict.
terms.explanation: Inline styles have higher specificity than IDs, which have higher specificity than classes and tags.

terms.title: Cascading
terms.definition: The process of combining different style declarations and resolving conflict between them.
terms.explanation: Determines how properties filter down through inheritance, specificity, and source order.
terms.example: p { color: red; } p { color: blue; } /* Blue wins */

terms.title: Inheritance
terms.definition: The mechanism where some CSS properties applied to a parent element are passed down to its children.
terms.explanation: Properties like color, font-family, and text-align are inherited by default.
terms.example: body { color: black; } /* Paragraphs inside body inherit black */

terms.title: Box Model
terms.definition: A fundamental concept where every element is represented as a rectangular box.
terms.explanation: Consists of margin, border, padding, and the actual content area.
terms.example: div { width: 100px; padding: 10px; border: 1px solid black; }

terms.title: Margin
terms.definition: Clears an area outside the border of an element.
terms.explanation: Creates space between the element and adjacent elements.

terms.title: Padding
terms.definition: Clears an area inside the border of an element, around its content.
terms.explanation: Adds interior space between the content and the element border.

terms.title: Border
terms.definition: A line surrounding the padding and content of an element.
terms.explanation: Configurable by width, style (solid, dashed, etc.), and color.

terms.title: Box Sizing
terms.definition: Defines how the total width and height of an element are calculated.
terms.explanation: 'border-box' includes padding and border in the element's total width/height.

terms.title: Flexbox
terms.definition: A one-dimensional layout model for arranging items in rows or columns.
terms.explanation: Offers flexible sizing, alignment, and distribution of space among items.

terms.title: Justify Content
terms.definition: Aligns flex items along the main axis of the current flex container.
terms.explanation: Values include flex-start, flex-end, center, space-between, and space-around.

terms.title: Align Items
terms.definition: Aligns flex items along the cross axis inside the current flex container.
terms.explanation: Values include stretch, center, flex-start, flex-end, and baseline.

terms.title: Flex Direction
terms.definition: Establishes the main axis, defining the direction flex items are placed in the container.
terms.explanation: Can be set to row, row-reverse, column, or column-reverse.

terms.title: CSS Grid
terms.definition: A two-dimensional layout system for web applications.
terms.explanation: Allows creation of complex layout grids with rows and columns simultaneously.

terms.title: Grid Template Columns
terms.definition: Defines the track names and size functions of grid columns.
terms.explanation: Accepts fixed values (px), fractional units (fr), or functions like repeat().

terms.title: Grid Gap
terms.definition: Sets the distance (gutters) between rows and columns in grid and flex layouts.
terms.explanation: Now standardized in modern CSS as the shorthand property 'gap'.

terms.title: Position Property
terms.definition: Specifies the type of positioning method used for an element.
terms.explanation: Common options include static, relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky.

terms.title: Relative Positioning
terms.definition: Positions an element relative to its normal position in the document flow.
terms.explanation: Offsetting it will not affect the layout of surrounding elements.

terms.title: Absolute Positioning
terms.definition: Positions an element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor.
terms.explanation: Removes the element from the normal document flow completely.

terms.title: Sticky Positioning
terms.definition: Toggles an element between relative and fixed positioning based on scroll position.
terms.explanation: Acts relative until a given offset threshold is met, then becomes fixed.

terms.title: Z-Index
terms.definition: Sets the stack order of a positioned element and its descendants.
terms.explanation: Elements with a higher z-index cover elements with a lower z-index.

terms.title: Stacking Context
terms.definition: A three-dimensional conceptualization of HTML elements along an imaginary Z-axis.
terms.explanation: Formed by specific CSS properties (opacity, transform, z-index) that isolate z-indexing within.
terms.example: opacity: 0.99; /* Creates a new stacking context */

terms.title: Media Queries
terms.definition: A CSS technique used to apply styles based on device characteristics.
terms.explanation: Enables responsive design by querying screen size, orientation, and resolution.

terms.title: Responsive Web Design
terms.definition: An approach that makes web pages render well on a variety of devices and screen sizes.
terms.explanation: Uses flexible grids, layouts, images, and media queries.

terms.title: Pseudo-class
terms.definition: A keyword added to a selector that specifies a special state of the selected element(s).
terms.explanation: Used to style elements based on user interactions, structural order, or state.

terms.title: Pseudo-element
terms.definition: A keyword added to a selector that lets you style a specific part of an element.
terms.explanation: Preceded by double colons (::), such as ::before, ::after, or ::first-line.

terms.title: CSS Variables
terms.definition: Entities defined by CSS authors that contain specific values to be reused throughout a document.
terms.explanation: Also called Custom Properties; set using double hyphens (--var-name).

terms.title: Var Function
terms.definition: Used to insert the value of a CSS variable.
terms.explanation: Takes a custom property name as an argument and optionally a fallback value.

terms.title: Transitions
terms.definition: Allows you to change property values smoothly over a given duration.
terms.explanation: Enables creation of smooth UI state shifts without complex JavaScript.

terms.title: Keyframes
terms.definition: Controls the intermediate steps in a CSS animation sequence.
terms.explanation: Defined using the @keyframes rule followed by percentages or 'from/to' keywords.
terms.example: @keyframes spin { from { transform: rotate(0deg); } to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }

terms.title: Transform Property
terms.definition: Lets you modify the coordinate space of the CSS visual formatting model.
terms.explanation: Used to rotate, scale, skew, or translate an element.

terms.title: Overflow
terms.definition: Specifies whether to clip content or add scrollbars when content overflows an element's box.
terms.explanation: Values include visible, hidden, scroll, and auto.

terms.title: Display Property
terms.definition: Specifies the display behavior (the type of rendering box) of an element.
terms.explanation: Common values include block, inline, inline-block, flex, grid, and none.

terms.title: Float Property
terms.definition: Places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text to wrap around it.
terms.explanation: Legacy layout mechanism; modern layouts rely on Flexbox or Grid instead.

terms.title: Clearfix
terms.definition: A CSS hack or technique to force a container element to automatically clear floating children.
terms.explanation: Prevents parent height collapse caused by child floating elements.

terms.title: Calc Function
terms.definition: A built-in CSS function that allows you to perform calculations when specifying property values.
terms.explanation: Combines different units like percentages and fixed pixels.

terms.title: Clamp Function
terms.definition: Clamps a value between an upper and lower bound.
terms.explanation: Takes three parameters: a minimum value, preferred value, and maximum value.

terms.title: Aspect Ratio
terms.definition: Sets a preferred aspect ratio for the box, which will be used in auto-sizing.
terms.explanation: Ensures responsive boxes maintain width-to-height dimensions (e.g., 16:9).

terms.title: Object Fit
terms.definition: Specifies how the content of a replaced element (like or
terms.explanation: Values include contain, cover, fill, scale-down, and none.

terms.title: Backdrop Filter
terms.definition: Applies graphical effects like blurring to the area behind an element.
terms.explanation: Used extensively for 'glassmorphism' UI designs.

terms.title: Filter Property
terms.definition: Applies visual effects (like blur, grayscale, and contrast) to an element itself.
terms.explanation: Adjusts rendering of images, backgrounds, or borders.

terms.title: Pointer Events
terms.definition: Sets under what circumstances (if any) a particular graphic element can become the target of pointer events.
terms.explanation: 'none' causes clicks to pass through to underlying elements.

terms.title: User Select
terms.definition: Controls whether the user can select text within an element.
terms.explanation: Setting to 'none' prevents text highlighting on buttons or UI controls.

terms.title: Container Queries
terms.definition: Allows developers to apply styles based on the size of a parent container rather than the viewport.
terms.explanation: Introduced as a modern CSS standard for component-based modular styling.

terms.title: Subgrid
terms.definition: Allows nested grid items to inherit the track definitions of their parent grid.
terms.explanation: Ensures descendant cards align perfectly to a master layout grid.

terms.title: CSS Modules
terms.definition: A CSS file in which all class names and animation names are scoped locally by default.
terms.explanation: Commonly used in build tools (Webpack/Vite) and frameworks (React/Next) to prevent global name collisions.

terms.title: BEM Methodology
terms.definition: Block Element Modifier is a naming convention for writing clean, modular CSS class names.
terms.explanation: Divides components into Block, Element (__), and Modifier (--).

terms.title: CSS Nesting
terms.definition: Native CSS feature allowing style rules to be nested inside one another.
terms.explanation: Reduces boilerplate code and brings preprocessor-like syntax natively to browsers.
